sections.title: Scalar Triple Product (STP / Box Product)
sections.content: STP of a, b, c is written as [a b c] = a.(b x c). It represents the volume of a parallelepiped with adjacent edges a, b, c. It is evaluated using a 3x3 determinant of their components.

sections.title: Vector Triple Product (VTP)
sections.content: VTP of a, b, c is a x (b x c). It lies in the plane of b and c. The expansion rule is 'BAC - CAB': a x (b x c) = (a.c)b - (a.b)c.

sections.title: Shortest Distance Between Skew Lines
sections.content: Skew lines are lines in 3D that are neither parallel nor intersecting. For lines r = a1 + t*b1 and r = a2 + s*b2, the Shortest Distance (SD) = |(a2 - a1) . (b1 x b2)| / |b1 x b2|.

sections.title: Equation of a Plane
sections.content: Normal form: r.n = d, where n is a normal vector. Cartesian form: ax + by + cz = d, where a, b, c are the DRs of the normal. Passing through point 'a' with normal 'n': (r - a).n = 0.

sections.title: Distance of a Point from a Plane
sections.content: The perpendicular distance of point (x1, y1, z1) from the plane ax + by + cz + d = 0 is |ax1 + by1 + cz1 + d| / sqrt(a^2 + b^2 + c^2).

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
1) Mixing up the BAC-CAB rule as (a.b)c - (a.c)b. It is strictly (a.c)b - (a.b)c.
2) Assuming lines are skew without checking if they intersect (if SD = 0, they intersect and are coplanar).
3) Taking the plane equation ax+by+cz=d and thinking a,b,c are direction ratios of the plane itself (they are DRs of the NORMAL to the plane).

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Level 2 introduces the Box Product (STP) and Vector Triple Product (VTP). In 3D, it expands to planes (normal vectors are key) and the most important JEE topic: Shortest distance between skew lines.

tricks.title: Coplanarity of 3 Vectors
tricks.explanation: Three vectors a, b, and c are coplanar if and only if their Scalar Triple Product [a b c] = 0. The determinant of their coefficients will be 0.
tricks.example: If [a b c] = 0, the volume of the parallelepiped is 0, meaning they lie flat on a single plane.

tricks.title: Cyclic Property of STP
tricks.explanation: The order of vectors in STP can be rotated cyclically without changing the sign: [a b c] = [b c a] = [c a b]. But swapping just two vectors flips the sign: [a b c] = -[b a c].
tricks.example: [i j k] = 1, [j k i] = 1, but [i k j] = -1.

tricks.title: Volume of Tetrahedron
tricks.explanation: If a, b, and c are the three adjacent edges of a tetrahedron originating from the same vertex, its Volume = 1/6 |[a b c]|.
tricks.example: If [a b c] = 12, Volume of Parallelepiped = 12, Volume of Tetrahedron = 12/6 = 2.

tricks.title: Angle between Line and Plane
tricks.explanation: If line has direction vector 'b' and plane has normal vector 'n', the angle 'theta' between the LINE and the PLANE is given by sin(theta) = |b.n| / (|b||n|). Notice it is 'sin', not 'cos'.
tricks.example: Line DRs (1,1,1), Plane normal (1,0,0). sin(theta) = 1 / sqrt(3). theta = arcsin(1/sqrt(3)).

tricks.title: Foot of Perpendicular to a Plane
tricks.explanation: To find foot (x,y,z) from point (x1,y1,z1) to plane ax+by+cz+d=0: (x-x1)/a = (y-y1)/b = (z-z1)/c = -(ax1+by1+cz1+d) / (a^2+b^2+c^2).
tricks.example: Direct formula skips writing the line equation and finding intersection manually.

tricks.title: Image of a Point in a Plane
tricks.explanation: Exactly the same as the foot of perpendicular formula, just multiply the RHS by 2. (x-x1)/a = ... = -2(ax1+by1+cz1+d) / (a^2+b^2+c^2).
